Proposition
[The inclusion of a regular level set is a smooth immersion]

↗ prop:regular-level-set-hypersurface-codim-one

In the situation of Proposition 12, the inclusion $\iota _c : f^{-1}(c) \hookrightarrow M$ is smooth, and its differential is injective at every point. Since $\iota _c$ is a topological embedding, $f^{-1}(c)$ is an embedded smooth hypersurface in $M$.

Proof

↗ prop:regular-level-set-hypersurface-codim-one ↗ def:level-slice-chart Read in the slice chart at $x_0$ and the chart $\kappa $ of $M$, the inclusion is $z \mapsto G^{-1}(\kappa (x_0) + \iota (z))$, a composite of an affine map with a smooth map; hence it is smooth. Its differential at the centre is $d(G^{-1})_{\kappa (x_0)} \circ \iota $. Here $\iota $ is injective, being a linear isomorphism onto $\ker df_{x_0}$; and $d(G^{-1})_{\kappa (x_0)}$ is injective because $dG_{\kappa (x_0)} \circ d(G^{-1})_{\kappa (x_0)} = \operatorname {id}$, which follows by differentiating $G \circ G^{-1} = \operatorname {id}$ near $\kappa (x_0)$. A composite of injective maps is injective. Finally $\iota _c$ is a topological embedding because it is the inclusion of a subspace.

□
